ai_assisted_workflow.heading: Master the Motion. Use AI to Accelerate the Workflow.
ai_assisted_workflow.copy: Build strong motion-design and compositing skills using professional animation techniques. Explore supported AI-assisted tools for subject isolation and workflow efficiency, then manually refine timing, masks, movement and visual consistency to achieve reliable commercial results.
foundations: Manual keyframing, temporal/spatial interpolation and Graph Editor curve crafting
Vector shape manipulation, Trim Paths, Repeaters and text range selectors
Mask feathering, alpha/luma track mattes and spatial alignment
Mocha AE planar tracking surface alignment and corner-pin calibration
Layer hierarchy, parenting rigs, and introductory expression controllers
Visual consistency: color matching, perspective alignment, and frame-accurate motion blur
modern_productivity_tools: AI-powered Object Matte for accelerated subject selection
Roto Brush 2/3 with Refine Matte edge boundary detection
Illustrator vector import with native SVG shape layer conversion
Enhanced Properties panel for streamlined parameter access
Essential Properties for creating modular, customizable composition instances
Motion Graphics Templates (MOGRT) packaging for Premiere Pro editorial handoff
Optional Adobe Firefly generative assets (concept exploration only)
quality_protocol: 1. Select subject using supported AI Object Matte or Roto Brush.
2. Generate initial matte and propagate across target frames.
3. Review hair edges, fast-moving limbs, and motion-blurred boundaries.
4. Manually refine edge chattering, flickering, and background contamination artifacts.
5. Freeze or cache mattes to guarantee timeline stability and render repeatability.
6. Verify visual continuity, lighting direction, and color grade across the full composite.
7. Conduct licensing and copyright checks for all external typography, audio, and visual assets.
8. Execute 100% full-resolution preview playback quality control before master export.
ai_assisted_workflow.beta_disclosure: Adobe After Effects AI Assistant and other emerging generative capabilities are introduced as optional awareness topics. Beta features are never mandatory for course completion or portfolio certification.

modules.module_purpose: Build a strong foundation in After Effects composition structure, animation concepts and project organization.

lessons.what_is_taught: Distinction between motion design, live-action video editing, and visual effects (VFX). Frame rates (24fps cinematic, 30fps broadcast, 60fps high-motion), standard delivery resolutions (1080p Full HD, 4K UHD, 9:16 vertical), composition duration, square versus non-square pixel aspect ratios, composition settings setup, and foundational animation planning.
subtopics: Motion design vs video editing: spatial graphic transformation vs sequential storytelling
Motion graphics vs VFX: graphic communication vs photorealistic plate modification
Frame rates and temporal resolution: 24fps vs 30fps vs 60fps motion smoothness
Resolution and pixel aspect ratios: square pixels vs anamorphic distortion
Composition settings: dimension presets, start timecode, and background color
Animation planning: creative briefs, story frames, and timeline mapping
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates properly configured compositions for landscape broadcast and vertical social formats.
lessons.why_it_matters: Incorrect composition settings lead to blurry exports, dropped frames, and distorted graphics.
lessons.expected_outcome: Accurate understanding of composition parameters and digital motion foundations.

lessons.what_is_taught: Comprehensive tour of the After Effects workspace: Project panel, Composition Viewer, Timeline panel, Properties panel, Effects & Presets library, Preview controller, workspace customization, and essential keyboard shortcuts for fast navigation.
subtopics: Navigating interface panels: Project panel, Composition Viewer, and Timeline
Streamlined editing using the modernized Properties panel for contextual controls
Searching and applying effects from the Effects & Presets library
Preview panel controls: frame skipping, resolution throttling, and RAM caching
Customizing and saving task-specific workspaces (Animation, Paint, Tracking)
Essential keyboard shortcuts: Spacebar, Home/End, J/K keyframe navigation, and Page Up/Down
lessons.what_learner_does: Configures a custom motion-design workspace and navigates compositions using keyboard shortcuts.
lessons.why_it_matters: A well-organized workspace and shortcut fluency double animation production speed.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fluid navigation of After Effects panels, tools, and playback caching.

lessons.what_is_taught: Layer architecture in After Effects: Solid layers, Shape layers, Text layers, Adjustment layers, Null objects, Precompositions, layer stacking order, layer switches, and introductory blending modes (Multiply, Screen, Overlay).
subtopics: Understanding layer types: Solids, Shape layers, Text layers, and Adjustment layers
Null objects as non-rendering spatial controllers for coordinated movement
Layer stacking order and optical rendering hierarchy
Layer switches: motion blur, adjustment layer flag, 3D switch, and continuous rasterization
Blending modes: light, shadow, and contrast math for visual integration
Introduction to Precompositions: nesting complex groups for timeline clarity
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a multi-layered scene combining solids, shapes, text, and adjustment layers.
lessons.why_it_matters: Proper layer choices prevent rendering bottlenecks and timeline clutter.
lessons.expected_outcome: Mastery of After Effects layer types, switches, and stacking behavior.

lessons.what_is_taught: Deep dive into the five basic spatial transform properties: Anchor Point, Position, Scale, Rotation, and Opacity. Anchor point relocation with the Pan Behind tool, transform relationships, spatial coordinates, and motion path visualization.
subtopics: The five core transform properties and keyboard shortcuts (A, P, S, R, T)
Anchor Point mechanics: the true center of scaling and rotation transforms
Using the Pan Behind (Anchor Point) tool (Y) to position centers accurately
Spatial coordinates: X and Y 2D plane mapping and pixel offset math
Proportional vs non-proportional scaling and negative scale flips
Visualizing spatial motion paths and curved motion trajectories
lessons.what_learner_does: Animates geometric elements while repositioning anchor points to create motivated swings and expansions.
lessons.why_it_matters: Misplaced anchor points cause erratic, amateurish scaling and rotation animations.
lessons.expected_outcome: Precise control over anchor points, transforms, and spatial coordinates.

lessons.what_is_taught: Keyframe mechanics: activating the stopwatch, setting keyframes, temporal placement, linear interpolation, basic easing shortcuts (F9 Easy Ease), navigating between keyframes, and creating basic movement sequences.
subtopics: Activating the stopwatch vs adding/removing keyframes manually
Temporal spacing: calculating duration and speed between keyframes
Linear keyframe interpolation: constant mechanical speed and its visual limitations
Applying basic Easy Ease (F9) to eliminate abrupt starts and stops
Keyframe navigation shortcuts (J to previous, K to next keyframe)
Assembling multi-property transform animation sequences
lessons.what_learner_does: Animates a series of graphic elements from off-screen entry to settled pause using keyframes.
lessons.why_it_matters: Keyframes are the fundamental building blocks of all computer animation.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fluent keyframe creation, timing adjustment, and introductory easing.

lessons.what_is_taught: Parent-child relationships, pick-whip linking, hierarchical transforms, establishing null controllers, group animation, inheriting position and rotation while maintaining independent local movement.
subtopics: Parent-child relationships: pick-whip linking and layer assignment menus
Hierarchical motion: how children inherit parent transforms without losing local offsets
Null objects as master animation rigs: controlling complex clusters cleanly
Separating translation from rotation by chaining multiple nulls
Practical use case: rigging a complex solar system or UI dashboard cluster
Breaking and reparenting layers across timeline segments
lessons.what_learner_does: Rigs a multi-element graphics cluster to a null controller and animates coordinated group motion.
lessons.why_it_matters: Parenting saves dozens of repetitive keyframes and enables complex motion choreographies.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to rig and control multi-layered graphic clusters using null controllers.

lessons.what_is_taught: Precomposing workflows, nested compositions, reusing modular elements, timeline organization, precomp navigation, viewport tabs, and troubleshooting common precomp pitfalls (render order, collapse transformations).
subtopics: When to precompose: grouping, applying effects, and timeline organization
Leave All Attributes vs Move All Attributes into New Composition
Navigating nested comps using the composition mini-flowchart and tab bar
Reusing precomposed design modules across multiple scenes
Collapse Transformations / Continuously Rasterize switch mechanics
Common precomp mistakes: nested timecode mismatches and accidental layer clipping
lessons.what_learner_does: Packages complex graphic sub-elements into organized precompositions and nests them into a master edit.
lessons.why_it_matters: Professional projects require clean, modular composition structures to stay manageable.
lessons.expected_outcome: Structured nesting and modular composition organization.

lessons.what_is_taught: Core animation principles adapted for motion graphics: Timing, Spacing, Anticipation, Follow-through, Overlapping action, Visual rhythm, and Motion hierarchy. Avoiding stiff mechanical motion in commercial graphics.
subtopics: Timing and Spacing: the distance traveled per frame defining weight and energy
Anticipation: small counter-movements preparing the viewer for major action
Overshoot and Follow-through: momentum carrying objects past their resting point
Overlapping action: offsetting layer start times to avoid robotic synchronization
Visual rhythm: matching animation cadence to narrative beat and viewer focus
Motion hierarchy: directing the viewer's eye to the primary message first
lessons.what_learner_does: Applies anticipation and overshoot to a geometric shape to simulate realistic physical weight.
lessons.why_it_matters: Design principles distinguish high-end broadcast motion from amateur digital slides.
lessons.expected_outcome: Understanding and application of classical motion principles to graphic design.

lessons.what_is_taught: Professional project preparation: deconstructing creative briefs, designing style frames, sketching storyboards, asset preparation, standardized project naming conventions, and disk folder organization.
subtopics: Deconstructing commercial creative briefs and identifying key messages
Developing concept style frames before opening After Effects
Storyboard sketching: mapping out scene transitions and durations
Preparing external raster and vector assets for optimal AE import
Standardized disk directory structures: 01_Projects, 02_Footage, 03_Design, 04_Audio, 05_Exports
Project naming conventions and version management (ProjectName_v01.aep)
lessons.what_learner_does: Sets up a project folder on disk and prepares style frames and asset bins for a commercial brief.
lessons.why_it_matters: Pre-production planning eliminates expensive rework and animation paralysis.
lessons.expected_outcome: Professional pre-production workflow and structured asset organization.

lessons.what_is_taught: In-depth breakdown of keyframe interpolation types: Linear, Bezier, Continuous Bezier, Auto Bezier, and Hold keyframes. Understanding the difference between temporal interpolation (speed across time) and spatial interpolation (path through space).
subtopics: Temporal vs spatial interpolation: time velocity vs spatial trajectory
Linear keyframes: mechanical, unaccelerated motion and when to avoid it
Bezier and Continuous Bezier keyframes for organic speed curves
Hold keyframes: instant step-transitions for typography and stepped animation
Keyframe Interpolation dialog: setting specific in/out tolerances
Fixing spatial boomeranging: removing unintentional spatial Bezier drift
lessons.what_learner_does: Inspects and converts keyframes across temporal and spatial dimensions to eliminate unwanted drift.
lessons.why_it_matters: Mastering interpolation types prevents erratic curves and delivers intentional motion feel.
lessons.expected_outcome: Complete command of temporal and spatial keyframe interpolation types.

lessons.what_is_taught: Principles of natural acceleration and deceleration: Easy Ease, Ease In, Ease Out, keyframe velocity dialog, percentage influence, peak speed control, and crafting dynamic acceleration ramps.
subtopics: The physics of easing: inertia, friction, and natural momentum
Easy Ease (F9), Ease In (Shift+F9), and Ease Out (Ctrl+Shift+F9 / Cmd+Shift+F9)
Opening the Keyframe Velocity dialog: incoming and outgoing speed values
Keyframe influence percentages: default 33.33% vs extreme 75–85% snaps
Crafting fast-in slow-out commercial transitions
Matching easing curves across multiple properties for unified visual velocity
lessons.what_learner_does: Configures keyframe velocity values to create high-impact, snap-easing motion graphics.
lessons.why_it_matters: Standard default easing looks generic; custom velocity creates modern, punchy animation.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to configure precise velocity and influence percentages for expressive easing.

lessons.what_is_taught: Mastering the After Effects Graph Editor: Speed Graph versus Value Graph, interpreting animation curves, adjusting curve handles, custom easing shapes, refining speed peaks, and diagnosing inconsistent motion.
subtopics: Switching between the Speed Graph and the Value Graph
Reading the Speed Graph: height equals velocity in pixels per second
Reading the Value Graph: slope equals rate of change over time
Manipulating Bezier handles to sculpt snappy acceleration ramps
Separating Dimensions (Separate X and Y) for independent value curves
Troubleshooting bumpy curves, unintentional speed dips, and sudden plateaus
lessons.what_learner_does: Sculpts custom Speed and Value graph curves to transform a robotic move into a silky, organic motion.
lessons.why_it_matters: The Graph Editor is the single tool that separates professional motion designers from beginners.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fluent control of Speed and Value graphs for bespoke curve refinement.

lessons.what_is_taught: Spatial motion path manipulation: Bezier motion path curves, spatial handles, editing paths in the Composition Viewer, Convert Vertex tool, curved trajectory design, and Auto-Orient along path.
subtopics: Spatial motion paths in the Composition Viewer: anchor points, tangents, and dots
Editing Bezier path handles directly in the viewer using the Pen tool
Using the Convert Vertex tool to toggle between sharp corners and smooth arcs
Auto-Orient: making layers automatically rotate to face along their trajectory
Spatial path refinement: ensuring natural parabolic arcs for organic motion
Converting vector mask paths into spatial position motion paths
lessons.what_learner_does: Draws and refines curved spatial motion paths and auto-orients an element along the trajectory.
lessons.why_it_matters: Real-world objects travel in curved arcs, not rigid angular vectors.
lessons.expected_outcome: Precision editing of spatial motion paths and auto-orientation.

lessons.what_is_taught: Advanced motion principles for commercial graphics: Anticipation, Overshoot, Follow-through, Secondary motion, Overlapping action, Staggering, Exaggeration, and Motion restraint.

Overshoot mechanics: calculating rebound decay across 2 to 3 bounce cycles
Follow-through: allowing appendages and secondary elements to settle late
Secondary motion: accent lines, particles, and subtle scaling during primary travel
Staggering: cascading element reveals by 2–5 frame offsets for dynamic depth

lessons.why_it_matters: Nuanced principles give digital interface graphics tactile realism and commercial appeal.

Placing timeline markers (asterisk / Numpad *) on rhythmic beats and musical transients
Sequential layer offsetting: cascading entries from left to right or top to bottom
Syncing animation hits and visual apexes to audio cues
Visual emphasis: holding still moments to give viewers time to digest copy
Matching transition speeds to the energetic tempo of commercial audio tracks

lessons.why_it_matters: Motion cut to music feels 10x more engaging and professional to commercial viewers.
lessons.expected_outcome: Accurate audio synchronization and rhythmic pacing across complex sequences.

lessons.what_is_taught: The finishing layer of motion design: enabling and fine-tuning Motion Blur, adjusting composition shutter angle and shutter phase, ensuring consistent easing curves across cuts, avoiding mechanical motion, and animation continuity.

Composition Settings Advanced tab: Shutter Angle (180° standard vs 360° cinematic streak)
Shutter Phase calibration for forward vs centered motion blur offset
Audit protocol for easing consistency: verifying matching acceleration curves across all active assets
Eliminating robotic dead spots and abrupt keyframe freezes
Visual continuity across camera transitions and graphic cuts
lessons.what_learner_does: Polishes a high-speed motion sequence by tuning shutter angles and aligning acceleration curves.
lessons.why_it_matters: Subtle motion blur and consistent curves make digital animation feel organic and cinematic.
lessons.expected_outcome: Mastery of motion blur mechanics, shutter settings, and animation polish.

faq.question: Is this After Effects course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The course begins with After Effects foundations and progresses into practical motion graphics and introductory compositing. Basic design or video-editing knowledge is recommended.

faq.question: What will I learn?
faq.answer: You will learn keyframe animation, Graph Editor controls, shape layers, kinetic typography, tracking, masking, rotoscoping, compositing and reusable motion graphics.

faq.question: What portfolio projects will I create?
faq.answer: You will complete a coordinated commercial motion capstone containing four assessed deliverables: a branded motion package, a 20–30-second typography promotion, a tracking/compositing shot and a reusable motion template.

faq.question: Will I learn logo animation?
faq.answer: Yes. Logo animation is part of the branded motion graphics package, alongside lower thirds, title treatments and CTA end cards.

faq.question: Will I learn professional animation techniques?
faq.answer: Yes. You will practice easing, Graph Editor control, anticipation, overshoot, follow-through, animation timing and motion polish.

faq.question: Does the course cover VFX?
faq.answer: It covers introductory compositing, masks, track mattes, basic tracking, rotoscoping, screen-replacement concepts and simple 2.5D integration. Advanced cinematic VFX is outside the scope.

faq.question: Will I learn AI tools in After Effects?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum introduces supported AI-assisted subject isolation and workflow improvements. Beta-only tools are optional and are not required for certification.

faq.question: Will I learn Motion Graphics Templates?
faq.answer: Yes. The course introduces reusable motion systems, Essential Properties and MOGRT workflows. Students submit a compatible editable template or documented reusable setup.

faq.question: Is Adobe Illustrator included?
faq.answer: Illustrator is a supporting application for preparing vector assets. After Effects remains the primary software.

faq.question: Do I need Premiere Pro knowledge?
faq.answer: Premiere familiarity can help with final editing integration, but advanced Premiere experience is not mandatory.

faq.question: Is Adobe software included in the course fee?
faq.answer: Software-license access depends on Nova Skills' verified training arrangements. Do not claim paid Adobe licenses are included unless confirmed.

faq.question: What is the difference between Premiere Pro and After Effects?
faq.answer: Premiere Pro primarily focuses on nonlinear video editing and finishing. After Effects specializes in motion graphics, animation and visual compositing.

faq.question: Will I get editable project files?
faq.answer: Students are required to create and submit editable After Effects projects, organized assets, reusable elements and documented final exports.

faq.question: What is the course duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course lasts eight weeks, includes 64 guided training hours and has a listed fee of ₹10,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.
